--- title: "Rapid automatized naming: objects sharing a phoneme" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · RAN_OBJETOS_FONEMA" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (B · Rapid naming; quality class B). Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea RAN_OBJETOS_FONEMA`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Denominación rápida de objetos (mismo fonema)*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/RAN_OBJETOS_FONEMA.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class B.** It has enough data to be described, but it lacks some of the guarantees of class A (stability across time points, item-level reliability or validity). Use with caution and not for individual decisions. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Rapid automatized naming: objects sharing a phoneme, from age 4 to 6 (8,414 administrations in 5 cohorts; 4 forms). Stability across time points ρ = .42. AUC .55–.73 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 1866 1868 1925 1926 | | Battery | LEEDUCA | | Format | rapid naming of a series | | Items | — | | Task family | B · Rapid naming | | Score | Time (s; lower is better) | | Instructions (platform) | En la pantalla aparece una plantilla con 5 filas que contienen 5 imágenes que se van repitiendo en cada fila, aunque variando el orden. La tarea consiste en nombrar las imágenes tan rápido como se pueda de izquierda a derecha, fila tras fila sin interrupción, tratando de no equivocarse. *(Spanish)* | ![Example of the screen format (2018 screenshot; not necessarily an item from this task).](../../figuras/pantallas/formato_ran.png){width=45%} ## Theoretical framework Rapid naming of pictures measures how quickly the child retrieves and says, in series, very familiar names; it is one of the best predictors of reading fluency. The variants change: - the **phonological similarity** of the names: same initial syllable, same initial phoneme, or unrelated names (control); - the **length** of the names: short or long; - **repetition**: five repeated pictures or varied pictures, on a card or one at a time. **What the evidence says:** - **RAN predicts reading, also with pictures and before reading.** A meta-analysis of 137 studies (28,826 participants) finds a moderate to strong relation (r = .43). Stimulus type is one of the most influential moderators [@araujo2014ran]. In a three-year longitudinal study, non-alphanumeric RAN measured before reading instruction predicted fluency growth, with no reverse effect of reading on RAN [@lervag2009ran]. - **In Spanish, pictures and alphanumeric stimuli form distinct factors.** In 874 Spanish children from Grade 2 to Grade 6, RAN tasks group into an alphanumeric and a non-alphanumeric factor, stable across grades [@rodriguez2015ran]. - **Phonological similarity adds a load that affects dyslexia more, but with letters.** Readers with dyslexia are more impaired than others when adjacent letters sound similar [@jones2013ran]. We have not found studies that manipulate picture names in this way: this variant is specific to the platform and its interpretation is, for now, a hypothesis. - **Format matters.** In Grade 1, serial RAN is more strongly related to reading than discrete RAN (one stimulus at a time) [@dejong2011discrete]. **What our data show.** These are class B and C tasks, with few sessions per variant: - **Stability.** ρ = .33 (control), .42 (same syllable) and .41 (same phoneme) across terms from age 4 to 6; .45 for the long versions at ages 7 to 8. - **Validity.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC from .55 to .72 at ages 4 to 6 and from .57 to .74 at ages 7–8. Against later low comprehension, only .52 to .63. Against Woodcock-Muñoz, maximum AUC of .70. - **Phonological similarity.** The same-phoneme version reaches .72 at age 6, compared with .65–.67 for the control, but the intervals overlap: there is no clear advantage in manipulating phonology. - **Caution.** Mean times change a lot between sessions of the same school year (in the control version, 25.5 s at 4.1 and 44.5 s at 4.2). Norms must be computed by session and the administered version reviewed. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Form| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|----:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 4.1| 1925| 2012| 154|2016/17 | 387| 387| 0| 17| | 4.2| 1925| 2012| 157|2016/17 | 360| 356| 0| 16| | 5.1| 1925| 2011| 153|2016/17 | 781| 0| 781| 34| | 5.1| 1926| 2011| 153|2016/17 | 895| 0| 895| 34| | 5.1| 1925| 2013| 628|2018/19 | 550| 314| 236| 30| | 5.1| 1925| 2014| 896|2019/20 | 237| 11| 226| 18| | 5.2| 1925| 2011| 156|2016/17 | 794| 0| 794| 34| | 5.2| 1925| 2013| 629|2018/19 | 492| 297| 195| 30| | 5.3| 1866| 2010| 140|2015/16 | 842| 243| 597| 36| | 5.3| 1868| 2010| 140|2015/16 | 851| 251| 598| 36| | 6.1| 1925| 2010| 152|2016/17 | 15| 13| 2| 3| | 6.1| 1926| 2010| 152|2016/17 | 914| 262| 651| 34| | 6.2| 1925| 2010| 155|2016/17 | 820| 251| 569| 34| | 6.2| 1925| 2013| 903|2019/20 | 476| 294| 182| 30| | Form| Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness|% floor |% ceiling | |----:|----------:|---:|----------:|-----:|-----:|------:|--------:|:-------|:---------| | 1925| 4.1| 387| 2012| 34.86| 13.82| 30.73| 1.72|NA |NA | | 1925| 4.2| 356| 2012| 61.77| 18.42| 58.20| 0.93|NA |NA | | 1925| 5.1| 325| 2013, 2014| 54.76| 15.09| 52.66| 1.04|NA |NA | | 1925| 5.2| 297| 2013| 43.05| 11.85| 40.85| 0.95|NA |NA | | 1866| 5.3| 243| 2010| 42.36| 14.07| 38.92| 1.67|NA |NA | | 1868| 5.3| 251| 2010| 35.59| 10.11| 33.62| 1.27|NA |NA | | 1926| 6.1| 262| 2010| 50.70| 17.34| 46.79| 1.39|NA |NA | | 1925| 6.2| 545| 2010, 2013| 43.97| 15.18| 40.59| 1.32|NA |NA | **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in seconds). Internal consistency from item-level responses is missing. As a timed task, stability is the preferred reliability estimate. | Cohort| From| To| n| r| ρ| |------:|----:|---:|-----:|----:|----:| | 2010| 5.3| 6.1| 1,520| 0.19| 0.20| | 2010| 5.3| 6.2| 1,326| 0.19| 0.20| | 2010| 6.1| 6.2| 812| 0.52| 0.54| | 2011| 5.1| 5.2| 1,452| 0.13| 0.13| | 2012| 4.1| 4.2| 352| 0.43| 0.50| | 2013| 5.1| 5.2| 400| 0.51| 0.55| | 2013| 5.1| 6.2| 334| 0.37| 0.40| | 2013| 5.2| 6.2| 316| 0.43| 0.45| ## Validity **Concurrent.** With other tasks in its own domain (Rapid naming (RAN)), r = .27–.75. Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Phonological awareness (4.1, r = .29); Vocabulary and oral comprehension (4.2, r = .20); Letter knowledge (5.1, r = .37); Phonological awareness (5.2, r = .34); Letter knowledge (5.3, r = .22); Word and text reading (6.1, r = .40); Word and text reading (6.2, r = .38). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .55–.73. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .50–.63. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_RAN_OBJETOS_FONEMA_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .53–.61 (5 time points; 220–464 children). ## Provisional norms | Form| Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----:|----------:|---:|----------:|----:|----:|----:|----:|----:|----:|----:| | 1925| 4.1| 387| 2012| 60.2| 52.1| 46.0| 39.9| 30.7| 26.1| 22.1| | 1925| 4.2| 356| 2012| 98.0| 88.3| 77.1| 71.0| 58.2| 48.5| 42.5| | 1925| 5.1| 325| 2013, 2014| 86.0| 72.0| 66.3| 62.5| 52.7| 44.4| 38.4| | 1926| 5.1| 895| 2011| 88.5| 81.4| 74.5| 67.3| 55.2| 45.5| 39.2| | 1925| 5.2| 297| 2013| 63.8| 58.1| 54.1| 49.2| 40.9| 35.4| 30.8| | 1866| 5.3| 243| 2010| 66.9| 59.0| 55.0| 48.1| 38.9| 32.6| 28.5| | 1868| 5.3| 251| 2010| 53.0| 47.7| 45.7| 41.5| 33.6| 28.1| 24.6| | 1926| 6.1| 262| 2010| 84.9| 75.0| 65.6| 56.4| 46.8| 38.6| 32.9| | 1925| 6.2| 545| 2010, 2013| 75.9| 64.7| 57.4| 50.0| 40.6| 33.5| 28.5| Each form (platform code) has its own norms, because the forms need not measure on the same scale. In rapid naming, less time is better: P10 is the time of the slowest 10%. These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_RAN_OBJETOS_FONEMA_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ### Forms: can they be pooled? Forms given at the same time point are compared. They are considered **equivalent** if the mean difference is smaller than 0.20 SD and the SD ratio is between 0.80 and 1.25. If the same children took them, **linear equating** is also computed, which puts the second form on the scale of the first, together with the correlation between forms (parallel-forms reliability). coding under review) | 6.2| 1,292| -0.034| 0.545| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 6.2| 1,293| 0.059| 0.034| |School (ICC) | 6.2| 1,296| 0.072| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Rapid automatized naming: objects sharing a phoneme” (codes 1866, 1868, 1925 and 1926; LEEDUCA battery) assesses rapid naming with phonological similarity. The child names a series of familiar stimuli on the screen as quickly as possible, and the examiner records correct responses and errors. The time limit is 60 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013 and 2014 cohorts it was administered in 11 sessions, from 4 to 6 years of age. The main outcome is the completion time (seconds). Stability across successive administrations (median interval of 4 months) was ρ = .41 (median of 6 session pairs; range .23–.45). Stability across time points was ρ = .13–.55. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .50–.63. ## Pending issues - Extreme value at 5.3 (form 1868): the maximum or minimum is more than 2 SD away from P99 or P1. Check in the raw data (possible timing or recording error). - The task has 4 forms; in 2 of 2 comparisons they have different scales. Norms are given by form (see "Forms"). - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
